title: Portrait of Natsume Soseki (夏目漱石), photographed September/October 1912
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, reproduced from National Diet Library digitized volume 'Soseki Zenshu, Vol. 8' (漱石全集. 第8巻, 1929)
licenseBasis: Photographer Ogawa Kazumasa (小川一真, 1860–1929); photograph taken 1912, published in a 1929 volume. PD in Japan (photographic works published before 1957/pre-1899 Copyright Act provisions; Ogawa died 1929, well past any personal-authorship term) and PD in the US (published before 1929 cutoff under URAA rules applied by Commons). Note: a near-duplicate/related capture from the same 1912 sitting is also on Commons as File:NATSUME_Soseki.jpg (823x1201, from 'Soseki no Omoide', 1928) with the same PD basis — not downloaded, kept as a documented alternate.
notes: Standard formal portrait; commonly identified as the type of photograph on which the old 1000-yen banknote engraving was based, though Commons does not explicitly document banknote-engraving provenance. Treat the 'basis for the 1000 yen note' claim as UNCONFIRMED — the note portrait itself is a separate engraved/stylized artwork (see rejected candidate below).

title: Calligraphy of Natsume Soseki — five-character kanshi (Chinese quatrain) with artist's seal, 1912 (Meiji 45)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons (privately owned original; photographic reproduction uploaded to Commons)
licenseBasis: Author Natsume Soseki, died 1916 → PD in Japan (50 years p.m.a. under the pre-2018 term that governed this work) and in the US.
notes: This is autograph brushwork (漢詩自筆) bearing his 漱石 seal, not a separate cursive pen 'signature' in the Western sense — closest available Commons asset to item 2 (署名/落款). Resolution is modest (320x1089); no higher-resolution version was found on Commons for this specific work.

title: Manuscript page of『吾輩は猫である』(I Am a Cat)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, reproduced from National Diet Library Digital Collections — 1936 'Soseki Zenshu' (漱石全集) published by Soseki Zenshu Kankokai
licenseBasis: Author Natsume Soseki, died 1916; work published in facsimile before 1931 → PD in Japan and US per Commons PD Mark rationale.
notes: Task asked for a『こゝろ』manuscript page or letter/kanshi specifically; no dedicated Kokoro autograph-manuscript file was located on Commons or via general NDL search in the time available. This is a confirmed, cleanly licensed Soseki autograph manuscript page (different novel) used as the closest verified substitute — flag for maintainer decision on whether a Kokoro-specific manuscript search (direct NDL Digital Collections browse of 漱石全集 volumes, e.g. https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1883350) should be pursued separately.

title: "I Am a Cat" (吾輩ハ猫デアル), English-edition binding/cover design by Hashiguchi Goyo, translated by K. Ando, 1906
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons, digitized from Yale University Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
licenseBasis: Designer Hashiguchi Goyo (橋口五葉), died 1921 → PD (published before 1931, and >50/70 years p.m.a. in Japan).
notes: Task asked specifically for the 1905 Japanese first-edition binding by Hashiguchi Goyo (大倉書店/服部書店 edition). No Commons file was found that is explicitly documented as that exact 1905 first printing; this is a 1906 English-translation edition that reuses/adapts Goyo's cover treatment for the same title, high resolution, confirmed PD. Treat as a documented substitute, not the exact requested artifact — a maintainer should check NDL Digital Collections directly (e.g. dl.ndl.go.jp holdings for 大倉書店 1905 吾輩ハ猫デアル) for the precise first edition if that distinction matters for the art pass.

title: Front cover, first edition of『それから』(And Then / Sorekara), Shunyodo, January 1910 (Meiji 43)
sourceCollection: National Diet Library Digital Collections (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/887086), mirrored to Wikimedia Commons as File:NDL887086 それから part1.pdf
licenseBasis: Commons file categorized PD-Japan and PD-scan (PD-Japan); NDL Digital Collections item is marked internet-public (protection-period-expired). Verified via Commons API extmetadata (License=pd, UsageTerms=Public domain) and independently confirmed publisher/date against the NDL bibliographic record (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/887086: 著者：夏目漱石 著, 出版者：春陽堂, 出版年月日：明43.1 -- i.e. author Natsume Soseki, publisher Shunyodo, Meiji 43 = January 1910), which matches the documented first-book-edition date.
notes: This is page 1 of a Commons-hosted, PD-Japan-licensed 100-page NDL scan (5983x4679 native page resolution, extracted at 300dpi via pdftoppm then cropped to the front-cover half of the two-page spread with ImageMagick -- a mechanical crop of a PD source, not a new derivative composition). Grainy bitonal microfilm-style scan typical of pre-1930s NDL digitizations, but this is the actual first-edition cover (title box + woodcut-style tree/sap illustration), not a later reprint -- confirmed against the 1918 Iwanami Bunko paperback reprint of a different Soseki title (Botchan) that was initially mis-identified as a first-edition candidate and rejected for that reason (see next entries).

title: Front cover, first edition of『三四郎』(Sanshiro), Shunyodo, May 1909 (Meiji 42)
sourceCollection: National Diet Library Digital Collections (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/886555), mirrored to Wikimedia Commons as File:NDL886555 三四郎 part1.pdf
licenseBasis: Commons file categorized PD-Japan and PD-scan (PD-Japan), extmetadata License=pd. Cross-checked against the NDL bibliographic record (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/886555: 著者：夏目漱石 著, 出版者：春陽堂, 出版年月日：明42.5 -- Shunyodo, Meiji 42 = May 1909), matching the documented first-book-edition date. Design attribution to Hashiguchi Goyo (橋口五葉, d. 1921) is the commonly cited designer for Soseki's Shunyodo bindings of this period but is not independently confirmed on the Commons/NDL file page itself -- flagged as unconfirmed attribution, not asserted as fact.
notes: Page 1 of a Commons-hosted, PD-Japan NDL scan (6039x4427 native page resolution, extracted at 300dpi then cropped to the front-cover half of the spread). Cover shows a thistle-motif woodcut illustration characteristic of Meiji-era Shunyodo art bindings, title stamped in seal-script.

title: Front cover, first edition of『鶉籠』(Uzura Kago), Shunyodo, January 1907 (Meiji 40) -- the collection volume containing the first book publication of『坊っちゃん』(Botchan)
sourceCollection: National Diet Library Digital Collections (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/885509), mirrored to Wikimedia Commons as File:NDL885509 鶉籠 part1.pdf
licenseBasis: Commons file categorized PD-Japan and PD-scan (PD-Japan), extmetadata License=pd. Cross-checked against the NDL bibliographic record (dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/885509: 著者：夏目漱石（金之助）著, 出版者：春陽堂, 出版年月日：明40.1 -- Shunyodo, Meiji 40 = January 1907), matching Botchan's documented first-book-edition date (serialized in Hototogisu in 1906, then collected into this Shunyodo anthology on 1 January 1907). Note: Botchan itself was not published as a freestanding first-edition volume -- its first book appearance is inside this multi-work Uzura Kago collection (with 'I Am a Cat' excerpts and other short works), so this cover represents Botchan's true first-edition binding rather than a substitute.
notes: Page 1 of a Commons-hosted, PD-Japan NDL scan (5862x4522 native page resolution, extracted at 300dpi then cropped to the front-cover half of the spread). Cover lettering is seal-script (篆文) style, publisher device at foot. Rejected candidates for a Botchan cover before this one: (1) 'Design title 1/2 Botchan.jpg' on Commons -- these are title-page ornaments from the 1918 English translation ('Botchan: Master Darling', tr. Yasotaro Morri, via Internet Archive), far too low-resolution (103x80 and 144x127 px) and not the Japanese original; (2) 'NDL1884801 坊つちやん.pdf' -- confirmed via its own cover page to be a 20th-century Iwanami Bunko (岩波文庫) paperback reprint (series no. 537), not a first-edition binding, so rejected despite being PD-licensed and high-resolution.
